title: Alpha release criteria + support readiness for Private VPC Terraform modules
creator: Vivek Kulkarni
description:
Context
We are targeting an alpha release of the AWS VPC Terraform modules to unblock regulated/enterprise Private deployments. In pilot discovery, the biggest failure modes are networking/DNS/endpoints/IAM mismatches and unclear ownership when something breaks. This ticket defines:
1) alpha release criteria (what must be true to label modules "alpha")
2) support model + escalation paths during design partner phase
3) what will be documented vs handled via Solutions Engineering / Pro Services (PS)

Related artifacts
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/private-vpc-terraform-modules-alpha-prd.json
- Module suite overview: sources/confluence/eng-infra/terraform-and-iac/vpc-terraform-modules-alpha-overview.json
- AWS reference architecture (EKS): sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/reference-architectures/aws-private-vpc-reference-architecture-eks.json
- Deployment guide (Terraform VPC alpha): sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/terraform-vpc-deployment-guide-alpha.json
- Logging defaults + SIEM hooks: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/private-vpc-logging-defaults-and-siem-hooks.json
- IAM boundaries guidance: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/private-deployments-iam-boundaries-terraform.json
- Upgrade/rollback runbook: sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/terraform-module-upgrade-and-rollback-procedure.json
- Alpha customer upgrade notes: sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/alpha-customers-upgrade-notes-vpc-modules.json

Alpha release criteria (must-haves)
A. Scope + module completeness
- Alpha scope is AWS-only VPC foundational footprint (no end-to-end app/cluster install).
- Module set published and versioned (tagged) in redwood-terraform:
  - core VPC/subnets/routing/NAT defaults
  - VPC endpoints module with documented DNS behaviors
  - security group patterns for expected ingress/egress
  - flow logs defaults + configurable destination (CloudWatch or S3) with secure defaults
  - IAM scaffold for installer execution role w/ permission boundary pattern
  - optional placeholders/outputs for VPN/DX (no hard-coded enterprise topology assumptions)
- Clear compatibility constraints documented (Terraform + AWS provider versions pinned per alpha).

B. Safe defaults + explicit supported topology
- Supported topology explicitly documented and validated:
  - 2–3 AZ standard layout (public + private subnets)
  - private cluster subnets supported; egress via NAT unless endpoints-only mode is explicitly configured
  - VPC endpoints list for typical private deployment (ECR/ECR DKR, STS, S3, CloudWatch Logs, etc.) with rationale
- Anti-patterns documented (examples): single NAT in multi-AZ without acceptance, missing private DNS on required endpoints, custom DNS resolvers without forward rules, broad 0.0.0.0/0 SG egress for nodes.
- Extension points documented (what customers can override without breaking support assumptions): additional endpoints, additional private subnets, custom tagging, alternate log destinations, custom CIDR ranges.

C. Validation + CI readiness
- CI gates in place and green on main:
  - terraform fmt + validate
  - lint (tflint or equivalent)
  - security scan (checkov or equivalent) with documented, reviewed suppressions where needed
  - provider version pinning enforced for reproducibility
- Integration test harness exists and runs on a defined cadence:
  - per-PR: lightweight validation (fmt/validate/lint/security)
  - nightly: ephemeral environment test (stand up/tear down) for the example VPC (cost controlled)
- Release workflow exists:
  - semantic version tags
  - changelog generation
  - clear guidance for alpha: pin versions; no implicit upgrades

D. Docs readiness (alpha bar)
- Deployment guide includes:
  - prerequisites (account/IAM, region/AZ constraints, quotas)
  - minimal inputs (required variables) and recommended directory layout
  - validation checklist before handoff to installer (DNS, endpoints, egress, logs)
  - troubleshooting for the top 5 pilot issues (initial list below)
- Reference architecture is consistent with module defaults and installer expectations.
- Support boundaries are clear: what Redwood supports in alpha vs what is customer responsibility.

E. Operational readiness (support bar)
- Runbook exists for:
  - module upgrade and rollback procedure
  - drift handling guidance and what is considered "unsafe" drift (routing/subnet CIDR changes)
  - collecting diagnostics (terraform plan/apply output, endpoint state, resolver rules, flow logs destination)
- Installer preflight checks aligned with module defaults:
  - missing endpoints / DNS misconfig should produce actionable errors (not silent failures)

Alpha success metrics (pilot-level)
- Time-to-first-successful installer run in a new customer VPC reduced (target: < 2 business days from AWS account access to passing preflight + initial install in design partner environment).
- Pilot reliability: < 2 P0/P1 network-induced incidents per design partner over 4-week pilot window.
- Supportability: >80% of pilot issues resolved using documented runbooks + standard diagnostic bundle (no bespoke debugging sessions longer than 60 minutes).

Support model (design partner phase)
Eligibility
- Alpha support is limited to selected design partners (tracked under PM-913) and Redwood-internal dogfood.
- Customers must agree to:
  - pin module version(s)
  - provide a dedicated technical contact + weekly 30 min check-in
  - allow sharing sanitized issues back into docs/runbooks

Primary support channel
- Shared Slack Connect channel per design partner (preferred) OR a dedicated email thread if Slack Connect is not possible.
- Internal coordination channels:
  - #eng-private-deployments (engineering triage)
  - #eng-infra (Terraform module owners)
  - #eng-security (IAM/logging/security posture questions)
  - #support (ticket intake + tracking)

Hours + response targets (alpha)
- Business hours coverage (Mon–Fri, local time per owner) with best-effort.
- Target response times (not contractual):
  - P0 (deployment down / blocking pilot): acknowledge < 2 hours during business hours
  - P1 (major degradation/blocker with workaround): acknowledge < 1 business day
  - P2/P3: acknowledge within 2 business days

Escalation paths (who owns what)
- First line (triage + intake): Solutions Engineering lead for the pilot (Markus Klein) + assigned SE (e.g., Colin O'Donnell)
- Infra module escalation: Irene Choi (owner) / Victor Alvarez (networking)
- Private deployments/installer escalation: Nina Petrova + oncall rotation for private installer team (via SRE if needed)
- Security escalation:
  - IAM boundary/policies: Marcus Lin / Hanae Suzuki
  - logging/SIEM questions: Kevin Osei / Allison Grant
- SRE escalation for outages / repeated failures: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes

Definition of severity (alpha)
- P0: active pilot blocked with no workaround, or suspected security risk (e.g., unexpected public egress path) requiring immediate action.
- P1: pilot blocked but workaround exists, or repeated failures in preflight/installer due to module defaults.
- P2: docs gaps, papercuts, non-blocking feature requests.
- P3: cosmetic issues, nice-to-haves.

Top pilot issues to explicitly document (initial)
1) ECR image pulls failing due to missing endpoints/private DNS configuration
2) DNS resolution intermittency in private subnets (resolver rules, DHCP options, outbound resolver, node local DNS)
3) NAT gateway AZ assumptions / route table mapping errors in multi-AZ environments
4) Flow logs destination permissions/retention confusion (customer-owned bucket vs CW logs)
5) IAM role boundary conflicts with customer org SCPs / permission boundaries

What will be documented vs handled as PS engagement
Documented (self-serve) in alpha
- Standard supported topology and minimal required variables
- Endpoint list required for common private mode + how to validate endpoint private DNS
- Baseline SG patterns and required ports between installer, cluster nodes, and AWS services
- Default logging posture and how to route logs to customer SIEM (patterns, not bespoke integrations)
- Upgrade/rollback procedure, version pinning, and known risky changes

Handled via PS/SE (by default) during alpha
- Custom enterprise network integration work:
  - VPN/DX design, BGP routing, transit gateway complex setups
  - custom DNS forwarding across multiple domains/forests (e.g., split-horizon, conditional forwarders)
  - proxy/egress gateway patterns beyond standard NAT (explicit proxy allowlists, TLS inspection)
- Non-standard subnet/IPAM constraints (e.g., extremely small CIDRs, strict subnet naming/tagging conventions that break assumptions)
- Customer-specific compliance requirements that require bespoke logging pipelines or retention beyond defaults
- Multi-account / multi-VPC architectures requiring shared services VPC patterns (we can provide guidance, but not a supported alpha module path)

Acceptance checklist to mark "Alpha Release Ready"
- Release tag cut for redwood-terraform modules with changelog
- Confluence docs updated + links from docs site quickstart where applicable
- CI green on main for 7 consecutive days (or 5 business days), including at least one successful nightly integration test run
- Installer preflight checks aligned with required endpoints + DNS expectations
- Support runbook published and reviewed by SRE + Support (Sean/Rafael + Support lead)
- Security sign-off for:
  - logging defaults + retention recommendations (Naomi Feldman / Kevin Osei)
  - IAM boundary approach + least privilege scaffolding (Marcus Lin)
- Design partner comms package ready (what’s alpha, how to file issues, how to pin versions)

Open questions / decisions needed
- Do we require flow logs enabled by default for alpha, or allow opt-out with a documented warning? (Security preference: on by default; SE preference: allow opt-out for cost in sandbox accounts.)
- Should nightly integration tests be mandatory before cutting a release tag, or acceptable to cut if per-PR checks are green and last nightly was <72 hours ago?
- Single NAT vs per-AZ NAT default: default should be per-AZ for reliability; document cost trade-off and supported override.
